 Pierre man and woman indicted for allegedly collecting dead husband’s Social Security payments 
 By Avery Arens Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 12:08 PM CDT | Updated : 31 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (Dakota News Now) - A Pierre man and woman have been indicted on federal fraud charges for allegedly concealing a death to keep collecting Social Security disability payments.
 51-year-old Beth Miley and 54-year-old Jason Miley were indicted in October 2025 and charged with Conspiracy to Defraud the United States, Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud, and Bank Fraud.
 The indictment states that Beth Miley hid the death of her husband from the Social Security Administration so that she could continue to collect her deceased husband’s monthly SSA disability payments.
 The indictment also alleges that between January 2024 and May 2026, Beth and Jason Miley made fraudulent monthly bank withdrawals of SSA disability payments from a bank account that wasn’t owned by either of them.
 If they are convicted, the maximum penalty would be 30 years in federal prison and/or a $250,000 fine. 
 Beth and Jason Miley were released on bond pending trial. A trial date has been set for December 15, 2026.
